answer: One concrete mechanism: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because mesa only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice falcon is enforced by the ledger itself: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any umber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
